reason: Driven, not read, and it reproduces exactly as stated. At ?state=owner-draft the surface is correct - .b-shared 'Only you can see this', primary verb 'Publish', stamp 'Updated 16 July 2026'. Pressing that screen's own Publish lands on states.publish with h1.b-pressTitle reading 'Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.' - the published branch, dated the day BEFORE the stamp on the screen the press came from - and 'Back to the plan' then returns 'Live since 15 July - anyone with the link can read it', verb 'Get the link', stamp reverted to 'Updated 15 July 2026'. Cause is exactly as the finding names it: render-b.js:1430-1434 sets F.publication/F.updatedLabel to the draft record, renders, then restores the seeded published record on the same tick, so every screen reached FROM owner-draft reads the published record. I drove the other path to test the 'it is only a fixture' defence and it does not hold. The real first run (owner-empty, set the day, Add a moment) commits the draft record before go() at render-b.js:1481-1482, and the whole chain stays honest: publish reads 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.', back to the plan stays 'Only you can see this', stamp stays today. So the product's logic is right and only the fourteenth state lies - which means the sentence written for this branch, 'Send it to Mara & Finn.', is unreachable on the one route the panel grades and the shots capture (approach-owner-draft is a captured frame; there is no draft-branch publish frame). Not a fixture legitimately representing an already-shared plan: both screens are the same record in the same session two seconds apart, and the false one back-dates a handover to before the true screen's own stamp. Not already handled (the correct path is a different project), not a gate restatement (interaction-check.mjs never mentions owner-draft in its 605 assertions), no constraint touched, and it is the 'self-contradicting facts' class from lessons.md creeping back across a navigation instead of within one screen - at the state whose own kicker is 'the moment it becomes theirs'. I tested the fix rather than trusting it: committing the draft record in the page and re-driving gives 'Send it to Mara & Finn.' on publish and a plan that stays 'Only you can see this' on return, with no other surface harmed.
sharpenedFix: Half the proposed fix is right and half rests on a false premise. Right half: in render-b.js states["owner-draft"], commit instead of borrowing - keep F.publication = { state: "draft", publishedAt: null } and F.updatedLabel = today's medium date, and delete the two restoring assignments at line 1434 (F.publication = was; F.updatedLabel = wasLabel). Verified by simulation: publish then paints 'Send it to Mara & Finn.', return keeps 'Only you can see this' and today's stamp. False premise: owner-empty does NOT restore the seeded record anywhere - there is no reset in fixture.js, render-core.js or render-b.js, it simply overwrites F.project/F.milestones/F.publication and never puts them back. So do not add a restore-on-entry-to-another-project rule; it is machinery for a navigation that does not exist. It is unnecessary anyway: every state is entered by a fresh page load (interaction-check.mjs open() makes a new page per state, and the shot harness likewise), so a committed mutation cannot leak into any other graded frame. The only in-session consequence is that Preview/desk reached from owner-draft carries 'Updated 16 July 2026' instead of 15 July, which is the correct stamp for a plan drafted today. One thing to know before shipping it: the draft-to-published flip is currently unreachable in any case - the 'copy' branch in wireOwner (render-b.js:1149-1157) that flips the record is bound only to the owner surface, while the only [data-act="copy"] control lives in states.publish, whose node has its own handler that never touches F.publication. I confirmed by clicking Copy the link on the first-run publish screen: the record stays draft. That is a separate defect and this fix neither causes nor cures it, but after this fix the draft branch becomes a terminus until it is fixed too.
